android.desc:
Switch on a retro TV set and see what comes on. Random TV Time plays classic movies, old cartoons, silent films, vintage commercials, newsreels and television taped off the air decades ago, at random, from the public collections of the Internet Archive. It is free, with no account, no sign-in and no ads.

WHY PEOPLE LIKE IT
There is nothing to search and nothing to pick. You turn the set on, sit through a moment of static, and something is on: a feature film from 1948, a cartoon short, a commercial break from 1996, a silent picture from 1912, a game show, somebody's home movie. If you do not like it, change the channel. It is channel surfing the way it used to feel, with a century of television and film behind the dial.

SEVENTEEN CHANNELS
The sets. Default is the tweakable set, with the look, the screen fit, the static and the hiss all adjustable in Settings. Cartoons plays cartoons and animated shows with the loud, splashy look of Saturday morning television. Silent Pictures plays films from 1910 to 1926 in sepia with grain, flicker and title cards. Classic Films plays features from 1933 to 1986 in a dark gold and cream movie channel look. Film Noir plays crime pictures of the 1940s and 1950s in hard black and white. Cable TV plays television from 1990 to 2019 behind a navy banner and bold white type.

The decades. A set for each decade from the 1950s to the 1990s, each drawn as a television of its years: a blond tabletop set in black and white, a walnut console, a harvest gold portable, a black set with a VCR readout and tracking lines, and a charcoal grey set with a blue input box.

SUPER FUN RANDOM TV TIME. Commercials, nothing but old ads one after another. News and Newsreels. Old Sports, games and bouts recorded off television. Game Shows, inside a marquee of chasing bulbs. Public Access and Home Movies, with a camcorder date stamp. Late Night, with creature features, science fiction and thrillers after midnight.

HOW IT WORKS
Swipe up for the next channel and down to go back to the last one, right where it left off. Swipe right to save a channel you like and left to let it go; your saved channels keep their links. Tap for sound. Double tap for the lineup of everything that has played. Tap the title of whatever is on to open its page on archive.org, or share it with a friend.
